chapter_theme: The excellence of rain (வானச் சிறப்பு): rain flowing with nectar makes every tree, sweet and bitter, bear nectar, and the Lord's clear river springs within the heart like rain falling from a mountain.

248.reading: Through the great rain that flows with nectar, nectar-bearing trees spring up on earth, areca and coconut with sugarcane and banana; even the bitter kanjirai is fed by it.
248.nuance: The bitter kanjirai (strychnine tree) in the last line may be named to show that rain feeds all alike, or the line may say the bitter tree too yields nectar. The verse doesn't judge between sweet and bitter.

249.reading: Like a waterfall of rain descending from the mountain, my Father's clear river springs up within the heart, beyond words, foamless, stainless, fine and without banks.
249.nuance: The rain becomes an image of the Lord's grace inside the heart; the yogic tradition may also read the mountain as the head and the stream as nectar from the crown. Both a devotional and a yogic reading stand.

links.note: Both call rain nectar (அமிழ்தம், அமுது): the Kural because the world is sustained by it, Tirumular because it makes the trees flow with nectar.
